title: Operator Administration Without SQL
objective: Authorized Oxford Lancers administrators can provision and manage application operators and their predefined role assignments through the application without requiring Brian to run SQL or make ordinary account changes directly in Supabase.
why_now: The authorization substrate, login and password recovery exist, but the hosted role catalogue and recurring operator-administration workflow are not available through the application. The approved Release 1 manifest marks Identity, Access and Operator Administration ready for intake, while current operation still depends on direct database changes.
non_goals: No runtime creation, renaming or editing of club roles or capability grants; the approved static 20-role catalogue includes the fixed coaching hierarchy
No wider H7 ownership and access completion sweep
No LAN-84 production recovery rehearsal or two-service-administrator establishment
No Meta, WhatsApp, DNS, Resend, SMTP, email-foundation or real-data cutover work
No player-facing accounts, persona-specific duplicate logins or public sign-up
No authentication-architecture redesign or operator two-factor authentication
No general People/roster redesign, operator self-service profile editing or player-facing authentication beyond duplicate-checked create-or-link Person needed for operator invitation
No coach module, coach self-service football workflow, expanded coach data visibility or unapproved coach capability grants; this mission includes coach account onboarding only
No special bulk handover mode or general cycle-open/close implementation
No full Stage-4 general change-audit browser, cross-system search, filtering, export or investigation interface; the bounded per-operator Access History is included
No Mission Lead DAG, worker assignment, detailed work package or implementation sequencing in this packet
No mission execution before Brian merges a ready packet version

requirements.text: The application uses the approved static 20-role catalogue: Operational Administration first (General Manager and IT Officer), Club Committee second, and the fixed ten-role Coaching Staff hierarchy third. The catalogue is available in hosted and local environments through versioned, reviewable repository artifacts and cannot be edited in the application.

Every operator-administration read and write is enforced at the server/service boundary by role_management plus target-level leadership and recovery guards. President, General Manager and IT Officer hold role_management. Vice-President and Secretary retain broad ordinary operating capabilities but cannot administer accounts or role assignments. General Manager may manage President; IT Officer may recover leadership email access but may not ordinarily assign, replace, end or deactivate President or General Manager.

The operator shell contains Operators and Roles destinations at /operate/admin/operators and /operate/admin/roles in Administration at the bottom of the left sidebar immediately above user/account controls. Roles are grouped in the order Operational Administration, Club Committee, Coaching Staff. The top-level role view shows role name, current holder and a useful read-only plain-language capability summary, without repeated year/scope labels; former holders remain on role detail. No role or grant is editable.

An authorized administrator first searches and duplicate-checks for the durable Person. If found, including a current or former player, the workflow links that Person; if absent, it creates a minimal Person using name and valid personal email only. The same guided flow requires at least one approved initial role, inherits the active operating year, defaults effective-from to today with permitted future/backdating, creates at most one operator login, and emails a secure invitation. Public sign-up remains disabled.

The workflow represents Invited, Delivery failed, Active, Deactivated, Email change pending and Reinstated states, treats invitation expiration as normal, permits correction and resend, and refuses duplicate Person bindings or duplicate emails with an actionable reason. Delivery failure preserves the same Person and operator account and never creates a duplicate.

The first version inherits one application-wide active operating-year context, such as 2026-27, for routine committee and coaching assignments. Forms do not ask for or repeat the year; the applicable cycle identifier remains explicit in stored state. Viewing another year requires a deliberate context switch, and historical years are read-only through ordinary administration. Missing, closed or ambiguous context is refused rather than guessed.

Ordinary roles inherit the active operating year and an effective-from date defaulting to today; future dates and audited backdating are permitted. No routine end date is requested. End assignment may schedule a future effective-to and requires a reason; replacement ends the outgoing assignment and creates the successor without rewriting history. General Manager is standing and single-holder; IT Officer is also standing; neither expires automatically at year end.

An authorized administrator can immediately deactivate an operator with a required reason and reinstate the same Person-account binding later. Deactivation prevents sign-in without automatically ending organizational roles, warns when effective roles remain, and never deletes Person, membership, binding, attribution or history. Reinstatement restores only capabilities from assignments that remain effective.

Forgotten password remains self-service through verified email. For lost or compromised email, an authorized administrator disables the old login path, records a reason, sends a secure verification link to an unused replacement email and keeps the account in Email change pending until verification. Failure is correctable and retryable on the same account. General Manager may recover President; IT Officer may technically recover President or General Manager without changing their authority; President may not recover General Manager.

No operator may deactivate themselves, end/remove their own role assignment or use the administrator recovery flow on themselves. General Manager may assign, replace, end or deactivate President; President and IT Officer may not ordinarily assign, replace, end or deactivate General Manager; IT Officer may not ordinarily assign, replace, end or deactivate President. President, General Manager and IT Officer may administer lower roles. No action may eliminate every usable administration path; General Manager replacement remains exceptional IT/service recovery outside this mission.

Every provisioning, account-state, email-recovery and role-assignment change writes one append-only canonical audit event naming actor, authority at the time, target Person/operator, affected role/assignment when applicable, operating year, timestamp, reason and before/after state. Operator Access History shows target-affecting events; role detail shows the role-related subset as holder history. The same event may appear in both projections without duplicate records. Ordinary page views and refused no-change actions are excluded; the full Stage-4 general audit browser remains excluded.

Exactly one owner-run bootstrap may establish the hosted role catalogue and first administrator-capable operator. It is reviewable, fail-closed, documented and audited. After bootstrap, every ordinary identity, access and role action is completed in the application; a second SQL-based administration touch is a defect.

A short club-facing guide explains duplicate-checked create-or-link Person, combined player/operator/role identity, guided email invitation, start-date behavior, active-year context, role assignment/replacement/ending, leadership safeguards, dual audit projections, deactivation/reinstatement and email recovery. It contains no SQL, Supabase-dashboard, administrator-created-password or WhatsApp-authentication procedure.

Implementation and verification do not alter hosted accounts, production data, secrets, email/DNS configuration or recovery ownership autonomously. Any migration or one-time hosted bootstrap remains an explicit Brian-run handoff under existing runbooks.

President, General Manager and IT Officer may assign people to the approved static catalogue, including roles that currently carry no privileged capabilities. Single-holder restrictions follow the constitution, with General Manager additionally single-holder; other roles permit multiple holders unless another authoritative rule says otherwise. One Person may hold multiple compatible roles. Administrators cannot create roles or edit grants in the application.

Administration visually separates Coaching Staff and supports duplicate-checked create-or-link Person, secure email invitation and active-year role assignment for every coach role. Coaching onboarding neither requires nor automatically creates player membership: an external coach may have none, while a coach-player links the existing Person and membership. One Person and at most one operator login may simultaneously carry player membership and compatible committee, operational and coaching roles. HC/OC/DC retain approved narrow attendance access; position coaches receive no unapproved capability.

Operator invitations, invitation correction/resend, password recovery and verified email re-home use Supabase Auth secure email links delivered through the provider-neutral transactional email path, currently Resend/custom SMTP under LAN-126. Administrators never choose or send passwords, WhatsApp is not authentication, and first login does not add operator profile editing.
